Verification accepts arbitrary string email and optional name without early email-format/name-length validation. RegistrationVerificationRequest and signed RegistrationKdf/Authentication/Unlock components have borrowed Deserialize implementations. RegistrationFinishRequest and RegistrationCredentials are explicitly programmatic semantic views, without a full RegisterData decoder or alloc-dependent untagged/flatten derive. The std host mirrors source aliases and tries a valid legacy variant before nested data, even if simultaneously supplied nested credentials are malformed. Caller-owned scratch or owned host decoding handles escaped strings; no no-allocator full-union parser claim is made.

Finish requires a sole ordinary email-verification token. Host normalization maps missing/mixed/unsupported organization/emergency proof tuples to no token while preserving credentials, so nested KDF/salt mismatch returns 422 before missing-proof 400. A valid legacy selection bypasses nested consistency checks. Nested authentication/unlock KDFs compare every signed/optional field before normalization; both salts must exactly equal raw email.trim().to_lowercase().

The provider verifies token signature, exact configured purpose issuer and NumericDate validity before returning an owned claims handle. Claim subject must equal raw finish email exactly, including case/space; persisted email uses Unicode lowercase WITHOUT trimming. Name comes only from claims, preserves Some(empty/control/Unicode), and is limited to 50 UTF-8 bytes at finish; missing name defaults to stored email for a new account. Finish body name, id, enabled, emailVerified and unknown fields cannot select persisted authority. Verification may mint a token for an invalid address; finish additionally requires adapter-supplied RegistrationState.email_valid after proof/name/hint/state/KDF checks and returns typed 400 before commit. The host uses pinned email_address 0.2.9 plus URL-domain/path/query checks matching User::save/util::is_valid_email, without introducing a core parser dependency or reusing its stricter ASCII validator.

Client hashes, wrapped keys and optional public/private strings are opaque, including empty/future values; this path does not invoke strict RegisterRequest base64/encrypted-envelope validation. Hint strings are Unicode-trimmed, blank becomes None and no extra maximum is imposed; the cleaned hint is checked against authoritative provider policy. Signed KDF 0 needs iterations>=100000 with no upper policy cap; KDF 1 needs iterations>=1, memory 15..1024 and parallelism 1..16. Other signed KDF types/iterations remain accepted, and every non-Argon type clears stored memory/parallelism. Portable HTTP exercises PBKDF2 success/retry and malformed Argon metadata; opaque/unknown signed acceptance and exact thresholds also use core/host tests, not a real Argon-client interoperability claim.

RegistrationStorage owns signup/password-presence/hint policy and deferred email validity, verifier preparation, UUID/time and an atomic validated commit. ValidatedRegistration is private-construction/redacted and only forwards canonical fields. Host rechecks private password absence and signup-or-pending-invitation eligibility inside the savepoint, stores an Argon2 verifier separately, persists account and private registration verification metadata together and never persists raw verification tokens/client hashes/nested request/unknown extensions in account JSON. Late account/metadata/commit failures must leave prior state intact; this host rollback boundary is stronger than upstream invitation side-effect ordering.

Private signing authority uses an independently persisted random 32-byte SQLite key rather than the access-token signing key; reopening can verify previously issued registration tokens. Host registration_jwt_is_purpose_bound_signed_and_uses_exact_leeway checks signature/purpose and 30-second boundaries with a supplied clock, not a live thirty-minute expiry wait. Host HMAC implementation is an adapter choice; tokens remain server-issued opaque credentials and are not claimed portable across signing authorities.
